parts.label: (a)
(a)(i)
parts.text:
Cell **X** and cell **Y** in Fig. 3.1 are sieve tube elements.
Explain why cell **X** and cell **Y** have very different appearances in this transverse section.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Sucrose is formed from the glucose synthesised by mesophyll cells in the leaves of *C. pepo*.
Explain how companion cells are involved in the transfer of sucrose into phloem sieve tubes.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Hydrogen bonding is important in the movement of water in xylem.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain how hydrogen bonding occurs between two water molecules.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Outline how hydrogen bonding is involved in water transport in the xylem of a plant stem.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Hydrogen bonding between water molecules gives water a relatively high latent heat of vaporisation.
Suggest why it is important to plants that water has a high latent heat of vaporisation.
